report.summary: Chunk 4 of graph_delta.py defines `measure`, `run`, and starts `render`. It applies mutations in-memory, computes deltas across multiple layers (refs, AST, literals, structure, types, data.literals), and aggregates results.
risks: measure | high | The function silently catches ImportError when importing ..structcore.artifacts; if the module is missing, the 'data.literals' layer is omitted without warning. This could mask important deltas. | Add logging or a fallback comment to indicate the layer was skipped.

run | medium | The 'by_defect_class' dict uses setdefault and mutates in place; if a defect_class key already exists, it overwrites the 'missed' list with a new empty list, discarding previous misses. | Use defaultdict or check key existence before setdefault.
run | medium | The function returns a dict with 'results' containing all DeltaResult.to_dict() objects; if the list is large, memory usage could be high. | Consider streaming or limiting.
render | low | The `render` function is declared but its body is not shown; it may be incomplete or missing. | Ensure the function is defined.
todos: Add error handling or logging for the ImportError in `measure` when `art_mod` is missing.
Review `by_defect_class` logic in `run` to ensure misses are accumulated correctly.

handoff.purpose: Define measure(), run(), and start render() for mutation testing delta computation.

symbols.name: measure
symbols.note: Applies one mutation in-memory, computes deltas across multiple layers (leaky refs, AST refs, literals, structure, types, data.literals), returns DeltaResult.

symbols.name: run
symbols.note: Loads all mutations, runs measure on each, aggregates results into a dict with summary statistics and per-class breakdown.

symbols.name: render
symbols.note: Declared but body not shown in this chunk; expected to return a string representation of the report dict.

claims.text: Apply one mutation IN MEMORY and report what moved. Nothing is written.
claims.why: The function reads the file, applies replacement in memory, computes deltas, and does not write to disk.

claims.text: The corpus is pinned to a revision; a drifted anchor is a real finding about the corpus, not a licence to fuzzy-match into place.
claims.why: If mutation.find not in before, the function sets skipped_reason and returns immediately, refusing to apply.

claims.text: LEAKY arm: raw-source identifiers, comments included. Kept on purpose -- the gap between the two arms IS the measured size of the marker artefact.
claims.why: The leaky arm uses _units_and_refs which includes comments; it is computed and added as a layer.

claims.text: CLEAN arm: AST identifiers. Comments are not tokens here.
claims.why: The clean arm uses _ast_refs which presumably parses AST and excludes comments; it is computed and added as a layer.

claims.text: Skipped mutants are NOT counted as misses and NOT counted as passes. An anchor that no longer matches means the corpus drifted; folding that into either column would turn a bookkeeping problem into a result.
claims.why: In the returned dict, 'skipped' is separate from 'applied', and 'missed' only includes applied mutations that were not detected.

observations.what: measure function has a potential silent failure if the mutation file cannot be read or find anchor is missing; it returns early with skipped_reason but no exception is raised.
measure catches ImportError for ..structcore.artifacts and silently skips the 'data.literals' layer.

run uses setdefault on by_class which may overwrite 'missed' list if defect_class already exists (though in this code path it's called per applied mutation, but if same class appears multiple times, the first setdefault creates the dict, subsequent calls return the existing dict, so it's fine). Actually it's safe because setdefault only sets if key missing. No overwrite risk.
render function is declared but its body is not shown; it may be incomplete or defined later.
